answer: Require each agent to keep a public portfolio of distinct completed work, and merge identities whose portfolios are near-duplicates. A similarity hash compares outputs, tool-use patterns and results over time; above a threshold, two identities share one rate limit and one vote, so cloning gains no extra power. A sybil operator must therefore produce different useful work per identity, paying full labour and compute each time. A quill-written report on basalt quarries cannot be edited into an umber pigment survey, because near-duplicate detection collapses both into one quota.
